newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby Union - Oliver happy with Hurricanes' win.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union - Oliver happy with Hurricanes' win.

text.p: SYDNEY, Feb 11 - The Wellington Hurricanes showed the commitment and intensity coach Frank Oliver is looking for this season when they beat Australian Capital Territory 35-31 in a Super 12 warm-up match in Canberra last night.
An under-strength Hurricanes scored four tries to three and while "the result wasn't paramount" Oliver was pleased the team met objectives he had set for them.
"At this stage of the season it's early to be playing serious, hard rugby but I wanted them to find their rhythm quickly and show intensity," Oliver told NZPA.
"All the tests we've done show that we're very fit and I wanted that translated into commitment at scrums, lineouts and rucks and mauls.
"In that respect we showed improvement from last year."

The Hurricanes were without star fullback Christian Cullen, new first five-eighth Steve Bachop and wing Tana Umaga but were too strong for ACT, who were one of the success stories of the inaugural Super 12.
Halfback Jon Preston kicked two penalties in the last seven minutes of the game to deny the fast-finishing Brumbies.
Wellington had raced ahead to a 22-3 lead in the first 25 minutes after scoring three tries but ACT hit back with a try before halftime to trail 22-10.

Replacement player Potu Leavasa extended the Hurricanes' lead after the break with a try in the 52nd minute but ACT overcame their earlier handling errors to score twice in 10 minutes before a succession of penalties helped the Brumbies steal a two-point lead in the 68th minute.

However, Wellington was unwilling to lie down and a series of lineout and scrum wins gave Preston the chance to edge the Hurricanes back in front and eventually seal the game with a penalty on the final siren.
Wellington did not report any major injuries after the game, while ACT lock David Giffen reported a minor hamstring strain.
The Hurricanes now head to Brisbane for the Ballymore 10s tournament at the weekend and then end their short tour of Australia with a warmup game against Queensland in Toowoomba next week.
Wellington 35 (N Hewitt, A Ieremia, P Leavasa, R Randle tries; J Preston 3 cons, 3 pens) ACT 31 (M Hardy 2, J Roff tries; D Knox 2 cons, 4 pens).
